name: The Atwood — Røknar House Spec
spec: 2 oz Røknar · ½ oz Sfumato · ½ oz Cocchi di Torino · ¼ oz Bénédictine · Peychaud's · Angostura · Saline
desc: Used Røknar Minnesota Straight Rye instead of Rittenhouse as the base. Røknar's grain-forward Northern smoke pairs distinctively with Sfumato's rhubarb smoke — a double-smoke pairing that works at the house level. Røknar is now the permanent house spec for The Atwood.
notes: Result: Absolute home run on first make. Røknar's smoked rye + Sfumato's rhubarb smoke = genuinely distinctive double-smoke pairing. Better than Rittenhouse in this specific context.

name: The Winnequah — First Make
spec: 1.5 oz Rittenhouse · ¾ oz Laphroaig 10 · ¾ oz Barolo Chinato · ¼ oz Bénédictine · Peychaud's · 3 drops Absinthe · Saline
desc: Solid on first attempt. Needs more reps — stir time and absinthe drops are the key variables causing inconsistency.
notes: Result: Solid but needs refinement. Trust the 40-second stir timer. Absinthe drops are the most sensitive variable — 3 maximum, use an eyedropper.

name: Cynar Neat — Digestif Evaluation
desc: Tried at restaurant digestif bar alongside espresso. Very close to Sfumato in profile — both earthy and bitter, Sfumato adds rhubarb smoke. Excellent at $12.
notes: Result: Buy it. Keeps coming up across multiple recipes (Black Manhattan variation, Mezcal Paloma). $12, every liquor store. The most deferred purchase in the cabinet build.

name: The Winnequah — Røknar Split
spec: 1 oz Røknar + ½ oz Laphroaig (replacing 1.5 oz Rittenhouse + ¾ oz Laphroaig) · everything else identical
desc: Triple smoke — smoked rye, Islay peat, and absinthe anise — may be extraordinary or may be too much. One deliberate trial needed.
notes: Hypothesis: Røknar's Northern grain smoke + Laphroaig's iodine peat + absinthe anise = the most smoke-forward version of this drink possible. Could be transcendent. Could be overwhelming. Worth finding out.

name: The Atwood — Amontillado Sherry Split
spec: 1.25 oz Røknar + 0.75 oz Amontillado Sherry · ½ oz Sfumato · ½ oz Cocchi di Torino · ¼ oz Bénédictine · Peychaud's · Angostura · Saline
desc: Most compelling unexplored Atwood variation. Nutty oxidative sherry against rhubarb smoke is a combination that doesn't exist anywhere else in the repertoire.
notes: Requires: Amontillado Sherry (Lustau or Tio Pepe, ~$25). Not yet in cabinet.
Hypothesis: The sherry's nutty oxidative character amplifies Cocchi di Torino's wine depth and creates a layered complexity that the straight rye version can't achieve.

name: The Atwood — Drambuie Swap
spec: Standard Atwood spec · Drambuie replacing Bénédictine · all else identical
desc: Drambuie (Scotch-honey liqueur) replaces Bénédictine's herbal sweetness with a whisky-honey character. All bottles in cabinet — low-hanging fruit.
notes: Hypothesis: Scotch-honey character pairs naturally with smoked rye. May create more coherent flavour through-line than Bénédictine's herbal sweetness.

name: The Winnequah — Cocoa Bitters
spec: Standard Winnequah · 1 dash Angostura Cocoa alongside or replacing regular Angostura
desc: Cocoa bitters may connect interestingly with Barolo Chinato's wine character and Laphroaig's smoke. Subtle change — worth a direct comparison pour.
notes: Requires: Nothing — Angostura Cocoa already in cabinet.
Hypothesis: Chocolate depth bridges the Barolo Chinato's wine bitterness and Laphroaig's smoke in a new direction.

name: Penicillin — Barrow Ginger Shortcut
spec: ½ oz Barrow Intense Ginger Liqueur + ¼ oz Barr Hill Honey Syrup replacing honey-ginger syrup
desc: Eliminates need to make honey-ginger syrup. More spirit-forward, potentially less sweet. All bottles in cabinet.
notes: Note: Barrow is 'intense' — may need to reduce to ¼ oz. Compare directly to syrup version on same night.

name: Mezcal Last Word
spec: ¾ oz Del Maguey Vida · ¾ oz Green Chartreuse · ¾ oz Maraska Maraschino · ¾ oz Fresh Lime
desc: Equal parts Last Word with mezcal replacing gin. All bottles in cabinet except Green Chartreuse.
notes: Requires: Green Chartreuse — not currently in cabinet. Yellow is not a substitute here.
Hypothesis: Mezcal smoke neutralises maraschino's sweetness in a way gin can't. The equal-parts discipline keeps any single ingredient from dominating.

name: Vieux Carré — Full Splurge Spec
spec: ¾ oz WhistlePig 12 Old World · ¾ oz Pierre Ferrand Ambre · ¾ oz Barolo Chinato · ¼ oz Bénédictine · Peychaud's · Angostura
desc: WhistlePig 12 wine barrel finish + Pierre Ferrand Ambre dried fruit + Barolo Chinato bitter wine depth. The highest-upside version of this drink.
notes: Requires: Pierre Ferrand Ambre (~$40). WhistlePig 12 already in cabinet.

Hypothesis: Three wine-influenced ingredients in a single drink — the Whistlepig's Madeira/Sauternes/Port finish, the Ambre's dried fruit, and the Chinato's Barolo wine base — should create remarkable layered complexity.

name: Spicy Mezcal Negroni
spec: 1 oz Del Maguey Vida · 1 oz Campari · 1 oz Ancho Reyes (replacing sweet vermouth)
desc: Bitter, smoky, and hot in equal measure. The highest-upside new agave drink in the repertoire. Unlocks the spicy category.
notes: Requires: Ancho Reyes (~$30). Not yet in cabinet — next priority purchase alongside Cynar.
Hypothesis: Ancho Reyes' chile heat + Campari's orange bitterness + mezcal smoke = a genuinely new flavour combination. The most compelling agave experiment pending.
